goal: Replace implicit default_board_viewer access with one explicit least-privilege viewer role through an owner-approved, atomic contract cutover.
runtime_artifacts: Reports, owner-approved manifests, backups and results belong under data/access-migrations/ with restrictive permissions; they are never committed.
The runtime role contract may be changed only by the dedicated audited cutover/rollback services with expected hashes and atomic replacement.
state_machine: Compatibility: while the valid runtime role contract lacks viewer, active users without an explicit contract role retain the legacy default_board_viewer profile.

Prepared: under one access lock and DB transaction, an active superuser applies a complete owner-approved manifest. The exact predefined viewer Group/Profile, selected memberships and approved Board ACL additions are staged and audited. Because viewer is not yet a runtime contract role, it grants no product authority and the fallback remains active.

Cutover: under the access lock, re-read actor, complete roleless cohort, viewer membership, technical flags, departments, customer-open boards, all relevant ACLs and hashes. If and only if they match the manifest, atomically add only the exact Git-default viewer role to the runtime contract through the staged SettingsChange writer.

Active: runtime viewer presence activates its explicit contract rules and simultaneously disables the legacy fallback. A user without an explicit contract role receives no role-derived general access.

Rollback: only on exact post-cutover state, atomically remove runtime viewer first to restore the fallback, then remove only migration-added memberships and ACL entries through audited domain services. Any later viewer/ACL drift aborts rollback.
authority: Report generation is read-only and does not require product-role mutation authority.
Prepare, cutover and rollback require a freshly loaded active superuser; is_staff or manage_roles alone is insufficient.
A roleless superuser may explicitly choose viewer, customer, another ordinary role or no_role; no choice is automatic and the existing superuser self-assignment rule remains intact.
Technical groups, is_staff and is_superuser are fingerprints and are never changed by this migration.
acceptance: viewer exactly matches the former read-only department-branch profile, contains the complete frozen capability catalog, protected=false, and has no write capability.
Legacy runtime without viewer preserves the current fallback; prepared inert viewer membership and ACL do not change effective product access before cutover.

The report lists every active user without an explicit runtime contract role, identifies technical-only users, and shows exact user and board/resource deltas for every allowed choice without a default.
The manifest requires exactly one explicit viewer, customer, other existing role, or no_role choice for every current roleless user and one explicit ACL choice for every customer-open board.

Prepare rejects unrelated pre-existing viewer Group/Profile, members or ACL references; it rechecks the complete cohort and board versions under the access lock, then changes memberships and ACLs in one DB transaction with AccessAssignmentAudit and BoardAccessAudit.
Prepare adds viewer only to owner-approved boards and preserves customer plus every existing valid ACL group; any user, department, group, board, ACL or contract drift aborts without partial state.

Cutover repeats the full manifest check and atomically adds only the exact Git-default viewer role to the runtime contract with backup, expected hashes and SettingsChange audit; ordinary role writers remain unable to change the role set.

After cutover no explicit role means no role-derived general access, approved viewer users retain the former read-only board scope, customer/other roles retain their defined access, and technical authority is unchanged.
A new or newly roleless active user between prepare and cutover aborts cutover; a new user after cutover receives no implicit product role.
Crash before contract replacement leaves the safe prepared state; crash after replacement is reconciled from SettingsChange. Retry is idempotent or fails closed on partial/inconsistent state.
Rollback removes the runtime viewer role before prepared DB grants and refuses any post-cutover viewer membership or Board ACL drift.
HTTP, effective-access explanation, selectors and UI agree with enforcement before and after cutover; the e2e command covers prepare, cutover and rollback.
non_goals: No persistent migration flag or new authorization-state model.
No automatic assignment to viewer, customer or any other role.
No direct unaudited user.groups or Board.allowed_groups mutation.
No deletion of arbitrary roles and no general relaxation of the frozen role-set writer.
